alerts.title: Viral load monitoring overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend viral load (VL) monitoring every 6 months for patients on DTG-based first-line ART, or every 12 months if VL < 50 copies/mL for >1 year with reliable adherence. The patient's last VL was 40 copies/mL on 2025-10-01 (113 days ago). The clinician's plan for 'routine follow-up' does not include ordering a VL test. A new VL test is now due to ensure continued virological suppression and adherence.

evidence.recommended_action: Order a viral load test as per the 6-12 month monitoring schedule for DTG-based ART.

alerts.title: Creatinine monitoring overdue
alerts.message: The patient is on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), which requires monitoring of renal function. The last recorded creatinine was 88 umol/L on 2024-10-01, which is 478 days (over 15 months) ago. No recent renal function test is documented, and the clinician's plan does not include ordering one. Regular monitoring is essential to detect TDF-associated nephrotoxicity early, especially as the patient has been on this regimen since 2023.

evidence.recommended_action: Order a serum creatinine test to assess renal function for TDF safety monitoring.

alerts.title: No documented ADR screening
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for each encounter, ALL health workers should screen for suspected Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) using a Drug Safety Screening checklist. The clinical note for today's visit only states 'No new complaints' and 'Appears well', with no specific mention of ADR screening. The patient is on DTG, which can cause neuropsychiatric symptoms (e.g., bad dreams, insomnia, headaches, mood changes). A systematic screening for these and other ADRs was not documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform and document systematic ADR screening using the checklist at every visit.
